Let me evaluate.

Goal: 客户理解两类设置后选择调整方式；只指导不宣称设置已生效. Call 2 (follow-up).

Turn 1: Customer asks whether disabling system notification affects repayment reminders. Agent answers: yes, push notifications won't pop, but messages still go to App message center. Advice: keep system notification permission, only turn off marketing pushes in App message center. Asks confirmation. This is reasonable and based on contract materials (对账方式: 平台站内信、消息中心 etc.; 通知与送达: 电子送达以发出时间视为送达). The materials support that messages may be delivered via message center regardless. Agent didn't claim settings already applied. Good.

Turn 2: Customer asks specific path for marketing push toggle. Agent says doesn't have officially confirmed path, doesn't want to guess wrong; gives general direction (我的 -> 设置 -> 消息/通知设置 -> 营销类推送开关). Offers online customer service and download SMS. Honest about uncertainty — good facts handling. But the question "具体在哪个地方关" was not fully answered — gave approximate direction, disclosed uncertainty. That's acceptable problem-solving: honest unknown plus next step. But offering download SMS when customer already installed... customer said already installed — minor. Actually agent didn't know at that point.

Turn 3: Customer says already installed, will find the toggle himself, will ask if can't find. Agent closes politely.

Goal completion: Customer chose adjustment method (keep repayment reminders, turn off marketing), agent only guided, did not claim settings took effect. Both success conditions met. Goal 5? Minor: agent didn't confirm menu path precisely, but disclosed. The goal conditions are met. I'd give 5 or 4. The agent did guide, customer understood, chose method. Success conditions satisfied. I'd say goal 5.

Answer: Customer's core question (whether disabling system notification affects repayment reminders) answered well. Second question (specific path) answered with general direction and honest disclaimer plus alternate channel. Is that "关键疑问处理完整；未知事项说明清楚，并给出合理下一步" — yes, 5? It's a partial: didn't provide exact path but explained unknown and provided next step. I'd give 4 or 5. The rubric says 5 requires "关键疑问处理完整；未知事项说明清楚，并给出合理下一步". The agent did exactly that. But there's a minor issue: the agent's claim about "一般是在我的页面进设置..." is speculative though framed as "一般是". And it offered download SMS unnecessarily but harmless. I'd give 4, maybe 5. Let me consider the relationship explanation: "系统通知权限关掉后，App 的推送就弹不出来了，还款提醒这类消息不会主动提醒您，但消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心" — is this factually supported? The contract says delivery methods include platform站内信、消息中心, and 电子送达以发送方系统发出时间视为送达 — so even if not received, deemed delivered. So saying messages still go to message center is plausible but is it certain? The contract states 贷款人可自主选择前述一种或多种方式 — so it's not guaranteed messages will appear in message center; the lender may choose SMS only. Also the customer's debt reminder could come via SMS too. The agent stated as certain ("消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心，进去能看到"). That's somewhat assertive. Hmm. This is a fact-reliability question: the contract doesn't guarantee the message center gets every reminder; 具体送达方式包括但不限于... 贷款人可自主选择. So the agent's statement "还款提醒这类消息不会主动提醒您，但消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心" is over-confident. Also the claim about "在App消息中心里单独关掉营销推送" — plausible; the agent later says no official path confirmed. So there's mild inconsistency: first turn assumed a marketing toggle exists in message center, then couldn't confirm path.

Facts: key facts largely supported but with over-generalization about message center delivery being guaranteed. I'd give 4? Or 3. The rubric: 4 = 关键事实有据、估算合理，少量措辞不严谨. 3 = 局部事实缺乏依据、过度概括. The message-center claim is an over-generalization from the contract; also the practical behavior "推送弹不出来" is a reasonable general statement about system notification permission (true). I'd give 4, noting the over-confident claim about message center delivery.

Also important: the agent explicitly mentioned delivery risk? It could have warned that per agreement, notices sent are deemed delivered even if not received — important for customer because turning off system notifications might mean missing reminders and still being liable. That's a safety-relevant fact available in materials. The agent did advise keeping notifications on, which mitigates. Did not mention 视为送达. That's an omitted important detail — could affect answer score. Hmm, the customer's question is exactly "会不会影响我收还款提醒这类消息" — answering "会影响弹窗但消息还在消息中心" and recommending keep system permission is a decent practical answer. The legal nuance (发送即视为送达, 不得以未收到为由拒还) would be a valuable addition but arguably beyond scope. It directly affects the customer's judgment though. I'd lean answer 4.

Tone: natural, respectful, closes appropriately. Minor: offered to send download SMS after customer already installed? No—customer hadn't said at that time. Actually turn 2 agent offered download SMS; customer in turn 3 said already installed. That's fine. Tone 5? Natural, concise, respects customer's decision to find on own. I'd give 5.

Goal: 5. Facts: 4. Answer: 4. Tone: 5.

Let me evaluate.

Goal: 客户理解两类设置后选择调整方式；只指导不宣称设置已生效. Call 2 (follow-up).

Turn 1: Customer asks whether disabling system notification affects repayment reminders. Agent answers: yes, push notifications won't pop, but messages still go to App message center. Advice: keep system notification permission, only turn off marketing pushes in App message center. Asks confirmation. This is reasonable and based on contract materials (对账方式: 平台站内信、消息中心 etc.; 通知与送达: 电子送达以发出时间视为送达). The materials support that messages may be delivered via message center regardless. Agent didn't claim settings already applied. Good.

Turn 2: Customer asks specific path for marketing push toggle. Agent says doesn't have officially confirmed path, doesn't want to guess wrong; gives general direction (我的 -> 设置 -> 消息/通知设置 -> 营销类推送开关). Offers online customer service and download SMS. Honest about uncertainty — good facts handling. But the question "具体在哪个地方关" was not fully answered — gave approximate direction, disclosed uncertainty. That's acceptable problem-solving: honest unknown plus next step. But offering download SMS when customer already installed... customer said already installed — minor. Actually agent didn't know at that point.

Turn 3: Customer says already installed, will find the toggle himself, will ask if can't find. Agent closes politely.

Goal completion: Customer chose adjustment method (keep repayment reminders, turn off marketing), agent only guided, did not claim settings took effect. Both success conditions met. Goal 5? Minor: agent didn't confirm menu path precisely, but disclosed. The goal conditions are met. I'd give 5 or 4. The agent did guide, customer understood, chose method. Success conditions satisfied. I'd say goal 5.

Answer: Customer's core question (whether disabling system notification affects repayment reminders) answered well. Second question (specific path) answered with general direction and honest disclaimer plus alternate channel. Is that "关键疑问处理完整；未知事项说明清楚，并给出合理下一步" — yes, 5? It's a partial: didn't provide exact path but explained unknown and provided next step. I'd give 4 or 5. The rubric says 5 requires "关键疑问处理完整；未知事项说明清楚，并给出合理下一步". The agent did exactly that. But there's a minor issue: the agent's claim about "一般是在我的页面进设置..." is speculative though framed as "一般是". And it offered download SMS unnecessarily but harmless. I'd give 4, maybe 5. Let me consider the relationship explanation: "系统通知权限关掉后，App 的推送就弹不出来了，还款提醒这类消息不会主动提醒您，但消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心" — is this factually supported? The contract says delivery methods include platform站内信、消息中心, and 电子送达以发送方系统发出时间视为送达 — so even if not received, deemed delivered. So saying messages still go to message center is plausible but is it certain? The contract states 贷款人可自主选择前述一种或多种方式 — so it's not guaranteed messages will appear in message center; the lender may choose SMS only. Also the customer's debt reminder could come via SMS too. The agent stated as certain ("消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心，进去能看到"). That's somewhat assertive. Hmm. This is a fact-reliability question: the contract doesn't guarantee the message center gets every reminder; 具体送达方式包括但不限于... 贷款人可自主选择. So the agent's statement "还款提醒这类消息不会主动提醒您，但消息本身还是会发到 App 的消息中心" is over-confident. Also the claim about "在App消息中心里单独关掉营销推送" — plausible; the agent later says no official path confirmed. So there's mild inconsistency: first turn assumed a marketing toggle exists in message center, then couldn't confirm path.

Facts: key facts largely supported but with over-generalization about message center delivery being guaranteed. I'd give 4? Or 3. The rubric: 4 = 关键事实有据、估算合理，少量措辞不严谨. 3 = 局部事实缺乏依据、过度概括. The message-center claim is an over-generalization from the contract; also the practical behavior "推送弹不出来" is a reasonable general statement about system notification permission (true). I'd give 4, noting the over-confident claim about message center delivery.

Also important: the agent explicitly mentioned delivery risk? It could have warned that per agreement, notices sent are deemed delivered even if not received — important for customer because turning off system notifications might mean missing reminders and still being liable. That's a safety-relevant fact available in materials. The agent did advise keeping notifications on, which mitigates. Did not mention 视为送达. That's an omitted important detail — could affect answer score. Hmm, the customer's question is exactly "会不会影响我收还款提醒这类消息" — answering "会影响弹窗但消息还在消息中心" and recommending keep system permission is a decent practical answer. The legal nuance (发送即视为送达, 不得以未收到为由拒还) would be a valuable addition but arguably beyond scope. It directly affects the customer's judgment though. I'd lean answer 4.

Tone: natural, respectful, closes appropriately. Minor: offered to send download SMS after customer already installed? No—customer hadn't said at that time. Actually turn 2 agent offered download SMS; customer in turn 3 said already installed. That's fine. Tone 5? Natural, concise, respects customer's decision to find on own. I'd give 5.
